open_issues: Official ArchiMate 4 Appendix B relationship rules still require a licensed profile artifact or redistributable non-verbatim derived data.

MEFF 4.0 namespace, Junction serialization, and multiplicity attribute names still require the official XSD; the official directory recheck on 2026-07-09 listed 3.1 XSDs but no 4.0 XSD links and tested 4.0 candidate URLs returned 404.
Exact C260 Appendix A vector artwork redistribution remains unconfirmed; current renderer entries use existing local paths or explicit aliases.
assumptions: C260 can be used as a local source for derived implementation requirements, but copied normative prose and Appendix B tables should not be committed without explicit redistribution rights.
The external relationship profile loader can validate the licensed artifact once it is supplied.
A licensed Appendix B relationship profile can now be supplied directly in Modeler or Viewer construction options.

Finite n..m multiplicity ranges, '*', and the input alias 0..* normalized to '*' are accepted from the C260-derived notation; non-zero unbounded range forms such as 1..* remain rejected until confirmed by MEFF 4.0 or another normative source.
Relationship popup options and reconnect validation now both use the active language profile, so a loaded ArchiMate 4 relationship profile affects editing constraints.
AndJunction and OrJunction are exposed as ArchiMate 4 relationship connector metadata outside the 42-element catalog until the official MEFF 4.0 exchange representation is confirmed.
Junction relationship type consistency can be enforced without embedding the licensed Appendix B relationship matrix.
Junction endpoint-chain validation now uses the active relationship profile, so final correctness improves when official Appendix B data is supplied.
Host applications can pass licensed Appendix B relationship profile JSON text without this browser-oriented package reading local files directly.

C260 Appendix E allows several migration replacements to be model-dependent, so the utility records alternative replacement types in warning data instead of silently implying a single normative target.
Specialization/profile migration metadata is stored through model Properties to avoid inventing a non-standard BaseElement specialization attribute before MEFF 4.0 XSD is confirmed.

ArchiMate 4 relationship and diagram connection descriptors use common abstract endpoint types so relationship concepts can participate in Appendix B.6 relationships while preserving ArchiMate 3.x descriptor behavior.
External Appendix B relationship profiles validate source and target keys against the accepted ArchiMate 4 concept set, including elements, relationship connectors, and relationship types.
Complete external Appendix B relationship profiles require explicit source-target cell coverage so omitted cells are distinguishable from empty disallowed cells.
ArchiMate 4 relationship profile status exposes fallback/external source and complete source/target-cell validation metadata so host applications can audit Appendix B profile coverage.
ArchiMate language customization is implementation-defined through archimateLanguageProfile; custom specialized concepts resolve to their standard base concept for relationship validation.

ArchiMate viewpoint mechanism support preserves viewpoint metadata and model-defined viewpoint definitions while example viewpoints remain informative and MEFF 4.0 exchange conformance awaits the official XSD.
Every ArchiMate 4 profile pictoRef now resolves to a renderer PathMap entry; several entries remain explicit aliases until exact Appendix A vector artwork redistribution is confirmed.
The ArchiMate 4 Deliverable profile now uses PICTO_DELIVERABLE while the misspelled PICTO_DELIVRABLE key remains only as a legacy compatibility alias.
ArchiMate 4 shapes now preserve profile domain metadata directly while retaining the legacy layer field as a compatibility alias.
Host-supplied licensed Appendix B relationship profile data can now be provided as a header-row matrix array while preserving complete source-target cell validation.
Host-supplied licensed Appendix B relationship profile data can now be provided as CSV/TSV matrixText while preserving complete source-target cell validation.
ArchiMate 4 relationship connectors use editor palette/color grouping metadata rather than ArchiMate domain metadata.
The official The Open Group XSD directory currently exposes 3.1 resources but no discovered ArchiMate 4.0 XSD links.
ArchiMate 4 relationship profile status now reports actual explicit target-cell coverage rather than the requested validation option alone.
ArchiMate 3.x to 4.0 migration now preserves explicit original domain metadata when replacement would otherwise lose domain intent.
ArchiMate 3.x to 4.0 migration can validate migrated relationships with a host-supplied Appendix B-aware validator and replace invalid relationships with Association by default.
C260-derived Appendix E migration now corrects Path-to-technology-internal-active-structure Aggregation relationships to reversed Realization before external Appendix B validation.

C260-derived Appendix E migration now warns, without automatic replacement, when Realization remains between Service concepts that came from different ArchiMate 3 domains because Specialization or Aggregation may be more precise depending on model intent.
Relationship-end multiplicity accepts 0..* as an input alias and canonicalizes it to *.
Influence relationship modifiers are preserved as arbitrary modeler-defined values, rendered when present, and editable through positive/negative quick actions.
Named ArchiMate 4 junction connectors retain the AND/OR marker and render an optional modeler-supplied label below the connector.
Connection popup relationship labels now use C260 direct and reverse role names while retaining the underlying standard relationship type for editing and persistence.
Imported Access, Association, and Influence relationship refs hydrate explicit accessType, isDirected, and modifier properties while retaining typeOption as a compatibility alias.

Edited Access, Association, and Influence relationship refs persist explicit accessType, isDirected, and modifier properties through create, update, and replace paths while falling back to typeOption only when the explicit property is absent.
The ArchiMate 4 palette exposes every standard 42-catalog element, including Common composite Grouping and Location, while ArchiMate 3.x profile palette exclusions remain unchanged.
The ArchiMate 4 profile uses the C260-derived standard display spelling Stakeholder and Course of Action while legacy renderer aliases remain available for existing 3.x metadata.
The C260-derived ArchiMate 4 element catalog fixture now guards standard display labels for all 42 elements, not only type/domain/aspect classification.
ArchiMate 4 metadata uses the C260-derived labels Implementation and Migration, Active Structure, and Passive Structure; ArchiMate 3.x compatibility metadata keeps the older local labels.

ArchiMate 3.x Physical concepts DistributionNetwork, Equipment, Facility, and Material migrate as same-named ArchiMate 4 Technology-domain concepts while retaining Physical as original-domain metadata.

ArchimateRenderer now resolves pictograms through the active language profile so ArchiMate 4 spelling-corrected pictoRef values and implementation-defined specialized concepts do not rely on legacy ModelUtil fallback metadata.
The public The Open Group XSD directory rechecked on 2026-07-08 still lists only ArchiMate 3.1 XSD links, so MEFF 4.0 XML details remain source-dependent.
Viewer and Editor demos are source-controlled under demo/ and require npm run demo:build to generate ignored demo/dist bundles.
Viewer and Editor demos now show ArchiMate 4 Common Domain notation with Common-colored local palette assets; exact C260 Appendix A vector artwork redistribution remains unconfirmed.
ArchiMate 4 C260 aspect labels Active Structure, Passive Structure, Composite, and Motivation require renderer border metadata to avoid invalid SVG rx/ry values.

ArchiMate 3 to 4 migration coverage is now dynamically checked against the current 3.x profile and 4.0 element/connector catalog: all 24 current 3.x-only profile types require explicit migration rows, and every default or alternative replacement must resolve to a 4.0 profile type.
C260 Appendix B.6 relationship-concept aggregation is implemented narrowly for Grouping, Location, and Plateau while the full table remains external-profile driven.
ArchiMate 4 element font glyphs are Fontello-generated from local renderer pictogram paths and fallback local shapes; exact Appendix A artwork redistribution remains unconfirmed.
Viewer and Editor demos now select ArchiMate 3.x or 4.0 through URL query parameters, with the unqualified demo URL defaulting to ArchiMate 4.0.
Palette icon rendering is profile-specific: ArchiMate 4.0 entries use fixed-size semantic SVG background-image classes while ArchiMate 3.x entries retain the existing SVG background-image classes.
Fontello element glyph classes remain available in archimate-font but are not injected directly into diagram-js palette cells because those glyphs overflow the 22px palette boxes.
ElementFactory is the runtime boundary for edit/display concept availability, and Importer propagates those active-profile errors to callers.

ArchiMate 3.x palette icon assets remain unchanged when selecting ?version=3.2; ArchiMate 4.0 adds dedicated local SVG palette assets for Motivation, Technology, Implementation and Migration, and junction fallback icons.
The context pad relationship arrow starts connect mode; users drag it to a target element, and the tooltip now says this explicitly.
The context-pad drag lifecycle creates an internal generic Relationship view connection, then opens the connection popup so the user can choose the final relationship type.

ArchiMate language customization now supports custom relationship objects that specialize standard relationship types; relationship validation and junction type consistency resolve those custom relationships to their standard base type.

Editor relationship menus now expand allowed base relationships into custom specialized relationships from the active language profile, and specialized relationships inherit base rendering and editable option behavior.
ArchiMate 4 relationship multiplicity popup actions now allow custom source and target values using the same C260-derived validator as persistence and rendering.
ArchiMate 4 Influence modifier popup actions now allow custom modeler-defined sign or strength values while preserving existing 3.x positive/negative quick actions.

C260-derived DR1 and DR2 are implemented as host-callable derivation helpers: DR1 specialization transitivity and DR2 weakest structural relationship derivation. These helpers return candidates and do not mutate models automatically.
C260-derived valid derivations DR3 through DR8 are implemented for host-callable dependency and dynamic derivation, including same-target opposite-direction dependency and Flow cases.

C260-derived PDR1 through PDR12 are implemented as host-callable potential:true candidates through derivePotentialRelationship(). PDR12 requires an external relationship validator before returning a candidate.
C260-derived in-line valid derivation chains are implemented through deriveRelationshipChain(), preserving source relationship ids and pairwise derivation rule labels.

ArchiMate 4 relationship profile status now exposes missing source and target-cell counts, and getArchimate4RelationshipProfileCoverageReport() lists exact missing source rows and source-target cells for host-side Appendix B transcription audits.
Custom ArchiMate viewpoint definitions now validate allowed element and relationship type names against the active language profile after custom concept and relationship specializations are merged.

getArchimate4ImplementationStatus() now exposes machine-readable status for the implemented 42-element catalog, active relationship profile, experimental MEFF 4 exchange boundary, local icon coverage boundary, and external-source blockers.
The ArchiMate 4 profile now records the C260 conformance requirement map as five required shall entries plus one optional may entry, with external blockers kept explicit.
Implementation-defined ArchiMate language profile attributes are now validated as typed profile attributes against active elements, connectors, and relationships.

getArchimate4ImplementationStatus() now exposes ArchiMate 4 source coverage so local C260/transcript evidence, W262 availability, Appendix B, MEFF 4.0 XSD, and Appendix A artwork-rights boundaries remain machine-auditable.
